subject: Cross-border streaming qualification & evaluation plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@medisync.health>, Tobias Klein <tobias.k@medisync.health>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-17T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Cross-border streaming qualification & evaluation plan

Hi Ellen / Tobias — great to meet you both on the call today. Quick written recap + proposed next steps so we have a single place to track the perf and residency asks.

Summary of what we heard (from Medisync):
- Target end-to-end streaming latency: p95 <= 250ms for single-turn short prompts (under 2s generation) and p95 <= 400ms for multi-chunk interactive sessions up to 60s.
- Concurrency: ~200 concurrent streaming sessions at peak across users in US + EU, with occasional bursts to 400 for 2–3 minutes.
- Sustained throughput: mixture of short interactive requests (avg 30 tokens) and longer syntheses (avg 600 tokens) — peak tokens/sec expectation ~12k tokens/sec global.
- Data residency: EU patient data must remain in EU region (no egress outside eu-central), APAC users prefer APAC residency where possible.
- TLS and customer-managed KMS for stored artifacts (audit requirement).

What Redwood proposes for qualification (high level):
- Pilot: 2-week regional pilot with three endpoints (us-west, eu-central, ap-southeast) running identical model variant and workload simulator.
- Acceptance metrics: p95 latency measured end-to-end (client->Redwood->response) below 250ms for short prompts in each region; <5% request error rate; concurrency sustain at 200 sessions for 30 minutes without degraded p95.
- Technical mitigations: continuous batching tuned per-region, prefix/KV caching for repeated context, model variant with 4-bit quantization for cost-friendly throughput on dedicated GPUs, and streaming chunk size tunables to trade latency vs throughput.

Immediate next steps we recommend (owners):
1) Medisync to confirm the representative test dataset & traffic profile (Ellen) — see attached template (medisync_streaming_requirements.xlsx).
2) Redwood to provide perf baseline and suggested sizing for pilot (Ben / Rishi) — attach: redwood_perf_summary.pdf.
3) Legal: exchange DPA addendum for EU residency (Connor to loop Legal + Tobias).
4) Schedule kick-off: propose 2026-08-24 for pilot start (Marissa to coordinate calendar).

Open questions for the pilot scope (please confirm):
- Are websocket-based client connections acceptable for streaming test harness? (we assume yes)
- Do you need packet-level latency measurements or will app-level p95 (end-to-end) be sufficient?
- Any additional compliance logs required beyond audit/auditlog retention (SOC2 already discussed)?

Attachments: medisync_streaming_requirements.xlsx (template), redwood_perf_summary.pdf (pilot sizing + expected GPU counts).

Thanks — I'll follow up with a calendar invite and the HubSpot playbook link.

Best,
Marissa Cole
VP, Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Cross-border streaming qualification & evaluation plan

Marissa — thanks for the concise recap and the template. A couple clarifications from our side:

- The 250ms p95 target is for the short prompts and is measured end-to-end (user device -> your endpoint -> model response). For multi-chunk interactive flows the tolerance is higher as you noted.
- Concurrency: 200 concurrent streaming sessions is accurate for our baseline; the bursts to ~400 are critical for product launches.
- Residency: EU user records must not traverse US regions. For APAC we prefer region-local processing but can tolerate cross-border if encrypted and covered by our DPA until we can host locally.

Two asks before we sign off on the pilot scope:
1) Can you confirm which model variant you'll use for the pilot (name + quantization level)?
2) Can Redwood provide an estimated GPU footprint and if there is short-term autoscaling to handle the 400 burst?

I've attached our filled streaming requirements sheet with sample traffic shape and a list of endpoints we'll use during the pilot.

Attachment: medisync_streaming_requirements.xlsx (uploaded)

Best,
Ellen Park
Director of Engineering
Medisync Health

Subject: Re: Cross-border streaming qualification & evaluation plan — technical notes

Ellen / team — looping in some technical detail so the pilot acceptance criteria are measurable and actionable. Quick notes:

1) Model variant & quantization
- Proposed pilot model: rw-gpt-large-v1 (production variant). For the pilot we'll use int4 quantized weights (4-bit) to maximize throughput while preserving quality. We'll also stage int8 if you want to compare quality vs latency.

2) Latency and streaming behavior
- Expectation: token emit time once generation starts ~10–25ms per token on our optimized runtime; however end-to-end p95 depends heavily on client network and chunk size. To meet p95 <= 250ms for short prompts we recommend chunk sizes of 16–32 tokens for interactive flows and aggressive prefix caching for repeated context.

3) Concurrency & GPU sizing (ballpark for pilot)
- Baseline concurrency target: 200 sustained sessions distributed across three regions. We estimate one dedicated A100-equivalent GPU can sustain ~80 interactive streaming sessions (int4) at the short-prompt profile.
- Suggested pilot sizing: 3 GPUs per region for baseline (9 GPUs total) to cover sustained concurrency plus headroom for bursts. With autoscale + burst capacity enabled, we can spin up additional GPUs to handle the 400-session spike; startup time for a warmed image ~90–120s, so we recommend using a small standby pool to shave scale-up latency.

4) Throughput & batching
- Continuous batching will batch small requests across connections per-region; batching window tuned to keep token emission latency low (<30ms additional). For the long synthesis flows we will allow slightly larger windows to increase throughput efficiency.

5) Data residency & encryption
- We'll pin EU traffic to the eu-central cluster. No EU user request data will leave eu-central during the pilot. For APAC: we can route ap-southeast traffic locally; if hostage to regional availability we will implement TLS + customer-managed KMS for any persisted artifacts. Audit logs with region tags available on Console.

6) Acceptance test harness
- We will run the harness from three runner locations (US, EU, APAC) and measure app-level p50/p95/p99, error rate, and token throughput. We'll capture raw traces for 24h post-run for root-cause analysis.

If that looks good, Ben and I will produce a short pilot playbook with exact test commands and Grafana dashboards by EOD tomorrow.

—Rishi
Principal Systems Engineer
Redwood Inference

- Successful EU-residency enforcement: no EU user data egress observed in audit logs.
